methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $35M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Remedy Robotics, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Bell and Jake Sganga, has raised $35M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company across the robotics sector, including peers such as Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics at Series B and Seed stages respectively.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the $35M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for progression from Series A, yielding $70M. Peer-median methodology references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.6B and a range of $1.1B to $1.8B, directly implying $1.6B.

The triangulated analysis produces a range of $60M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $860M across the two methods. This wide dispersion reflects material tension between the stage-progression method, which anchors to capital deployed, and peer multiples, which reflect market sentiment toward robotics assets. Key uncertainties driving the range include: the stage and revenue maturity of the peer set relative to Remedy's development; whether peer valuations reflect sustainable unit economics or frothy sector sentiment; and Remedy's specific product-market positioning within the broad robotics category. A defensible fair-value estimate requires additional diligence on revenue run-rate, customer concentration, and technical differentiation.
